question: If the numerator of a fraction is decreased by 10% and the denominator is increased by 15%, the value of the new fraction becomes (2)/(5). What is the original fraction?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the original fraction be N / D.

(100 − 10)% of N / (100 + 15)% of D = 2 / 5

90% of N / 115% of D = 2 / 5

N / D = (2 × 115) / (5 × 90)

N / D = 230 / 450 = 23 / 45

**∴ The correct answer is 23/45.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Decrease in numerator = 10%

Increase in denominator = 15%

Resulting fraction = 2 / 5
